properties.statement: CORRECTION TO fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server: THE STRANDED SESSION IS RECOVERABLE WITHOUT AN MCP RECONNECT, AND THE WORKAROUND IS ONE COMMAND. That node states the failure is 'unrecoverable for the life of the session — every later respawn resolves the same dead inode, and only a full MCP reconnect clears it.' The first clause is right and the second is WRONG, proven here on 2026-08-08 by hitting the failure and recovering from it mid-session. WHAT HAPPENED: after the shared daemon's binary was replaced by a `cargo test` relink, the daemon exited and the client's auto-respawn failed with 'could not spawn the shared reflow2 server: No such file or directory (os error 2)' — the documented symptom, including the misleading advice to check a server log that cannot contain the cause. THE RECOVERY, verified by execution: start a replacement daemon BY HAND from the on-disk path, `setsid nohup ./target/debug/reflow2-mcp --graph-path ./.reflow2/graph --serve-shared &`, and the next tool call from the SAME session attached to it and worked normally (claim_report returned, then mint_seat, claim_region, open_questions, and a dozen further calls). No reconnect, no session restart, no context lost. WHY THE ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS WRONG: it reasoned that because the CLIENT resolves the binary through `current_exe()` and that inode is dead, every attempt must fail. True — but only of the client's SPAWN path. Attaching is a separate act: the client looks for a published server for that graph, and a server started by any means satisfies it. The dead inode blocks the client from CREATING a daemon; it does not block it from FINDING one. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE WORKAROUND: 'unrecoverable, restart the session' is expensive advice for ephemeral seats that are already dying on context exhaustion, and it was written into the graph as measured fact on reasoning alone. The original node's own evidence field says the diagnosis was 'recorded in session handoffs as worth filing and still unfiled' — so the recoverability clause was inherited, never tested. NOTE THE SHAPE, which is the same one this file keeps producing: a claim that was true about one mechanism (spawn) stated as true about the whole situation (the session), with nothing marking which part had been measured.
